limitations: This create-only request is an explicit closure over the discovery assignment; an empty reviewer_added_requests array means no reviewer-added candidates were found.
Ranking evidence and candidate material fingerprints are copied exactly from the bound discovery capsule and do not replace final source review.

reviewer_added_requests.discovery_reason: AI code review explicitly escalates added or upgraded dependencies with known vulnerabilities, GPL or AGPL conflicts, and broad transitive attack surfaces. This candidate owns graph delta, reachability, malicious-package and install-time execution risks, license and provenance evidence, remediation, exceptions, and proof limits. Full material is needed to distinguish reachable diff findings from authoritative dependency-risk acceptance.

AI code review verifies referenced APIs and dependencies and treats dependency additions or upgrades as material compatibility and security risks. This candidate owns repository authority, capability rationale, resolved graph and lockfile delta, lifecycle, provenance, install side effects, compatibility, and removal proof. Full material is needed to assess whether dependency mechanics and AI-specific review responsibilities have a complete handoff.

Contract testing validates API payload, error, authorization, pagination, default, and compatibility semantics while explicitly excluding contract design. This candidate owns consumer and resource meaning, trusted context, request and response semantics, errors, repeat delivery, pagination, completion, and compatibility evidence. Full material is required to verify the boundary between designing an API contract and proving executable provider-consumer compatibility.

Contract testing covers event schemas, retained messages, replayed payloads, ordering, duplicates, and old and new producer-consumer combinations. This candidate owns event meaning, topology, consistency boundaries, delivery identity, ordering, replay, backpressure, compatibility, and failure evidence. Full material is needed to compare executable event compatibility proof with event-architecture authority and avoid treating broker fixtures as architectural evidence.

End-to-end testing models the final user or business outcome, durable side effects, forbidden effects, roles, tenants, and recovery branches. This candidate owns business vocabulary, invariant authority, transitions, enforcement, bypass paths, golden cases, and validation maps. Full material is needed to ensure an assembled journey proves an authoritative invariant without inventing or replacing its business meaning.

End-to-end journeys bind role and tenant context and require critical negative branches, while their references explicitly leave backend authorization completeness to the owning proof. This candidate owns subject-resource-action conditions, tenant scope, privilege transitions, enforcement, denial disclosure, delegated entitlement, and negative evidence. Full material is needed to define the exact boundary between journey proof and permission authority.

Frontend-testing reference material explicitly routes design-system state and accessibility decisions to this candidate while retaining component, route, browser, and observable-state proof. The candidate owns semantic intent, token and component mapping, variants, responsive and accessibility behavior, exceptions, and validation evidence. Full material is required to verify that tests prove accepted design rules rather than silently defining them.

Frontend testing covers browser routes, API-backed states, outbound requests, permission differences, redirects, and user-observable failure behavior but cannot prove backend enforcement. This candidate owns reachable browser and server sources and sinks, state-change integrity, fetch and upload boundaries, cross-origin behavior, denial, and bypass evidence. Full material is needed to separate browser test evidence from web-security authority.

Integration testing explicitly proves concurrency and eventual consistency through allowed terminal-result sets, forbidden durable states, duplicate effects, and bounded observation rather than scheduler interleavings. This candidate owns concurrent writes, critical sections, locks, leases, optimistic conflicts, and concurrency tests. Full material is needed to distinguish evidence at a real seam from the authoritative concurrency mechanism and its correctness limits.

Integration testing rejects positive-only authorization cases and stops when authorization ownership is unresolved, while asserting denial, caller response, durable state, and forbidden effects at real seams. This candidate owns permission authority, subject-resource-action conditions, tenant scope, enforcement, denial disclosure, delegated entitlement, and negative proof. Full material is needed to compare permission design with integration-level enforcement evidence.

Integration testing asserts rollback, independently committed and asynchronous effects, forbidden partial states, constraint failures, unknown outcomes, and cleanup beyond one transaction. This candidate owns transaction scope, isolation, locking, conflict handling, and consistency tests. Full material is required to verify where integration proof ends and transaction-consistency design begins, especially when a green response can hide escaped effects.

Targeted validation selects exact repository commands and interprets their outcomes after the final material edit, but command success may conceal stale generated artifacts, undeclared graph edges, environment inputs, or cache errors. This candidate owns build graph authority, generated sources, toolchain identity, cache and parallel correctness, artifact comparison, and failure evidence. Full material is needed to bound build-command proof.

Targeted validation records exact commands, real outcomes, freshness, side effects, and covered paths, while hosted checks may involve different triggers, credentials, runners, affected-work selection, artifacts, and promotion behavior. This candidate owns those pipeline enforcement and rollback boundaries. Full material is needed to distinguish local or task-level validation evidence from hosted CI and release-pipeline proof.

Test-data management reference material explicitly routes restore datasets to this candidate while retaining fixture meaning, isolation, namespace, cleanup, and freshness. The candidate owns recoverable-state inventory, restore objectives, artifact lineage, dependency order, restore validation, and proof limits. Full material is needed to distinguish a bounded test fixture or seed from evidence that a protected backup can actually restore usable state.

Test-data management reference material explicitly routes volume budgets to this candidate while retaining deterministic fixture generation, representative relationships, sensitive-data controls, and cleanup. The candidate owns authorized latency, throughput, memory, unit-cost, and workload budgets with measurement-integrity evidence. Full material is required to separate representative test-data scale from an accepted performance or production-capacity claim.

Test strategy stops when capacity risk lacks an accountable evidence owner and selects proof levels, commands, omissions, and oracles from named consequences. This candidate owns authorized performance and unit-cost budgets, representative workloads, changed-surface metrics, measurement integrity, correctness guards, and exceptions. Full material is needed to compare performance acceptance authority with selection of an admissible test portfolio.

Testability-seam design controls scheduling and nondeterminism while requiring substitutes to preserve ordering and concurrency semantics without distorting production behavior. This candidate owns concurrent writes, races, locks, leases, optimistic conflicts, queues, and their tests. Full material is needed to determine when a deterministic seam is valid evidence and when the real concurrency mechanism must remain authoritative.

Testability-seam design requires doubles to model authorization behavior and forbids test controls from bypassing validation, permissions, invariants, lifecycle, or production side-effect ownership. This candidate owns permission authority, subject-resource-action conditions, tenant scope, enforcement, denial disclosure, delegated entitlement, and negative proof. Full material is needed to verify that test seams preserve rather than redefine the trust boundary.

Testability-seam design requires substitutes to preserve transaction, error, timeout, cancellation, and cleanup semantics and routes claims needing a real dependency to integration proof. This candidate owns transaction boundaries, isolation, locking, conflict handling, and consistency tests. Full material is needed to compare seam fidelity with authoritative transaction behavior and prevent a convenient fake from proving impossible consistency.

Unit testing proves local rules, invariants, branches, denied effects, and falsifying cases but must not infer business meaning from implementation structure or fixtures. This candidate owns rule source and authority, conditions, outcomes, precedence, precision, exceptions, enforcement mapping, and unresolved terms. Full material is needed to distinguish extracting an authoritative rule from testing its local implementation.
